problemStatement.formal: For t >= 1 and A subset {1,...,N}, assume a,b in A with a < b and b-a >= t implies b-a does not divide b. How large can |A| be, and is |A| <= (1/2 + o_t(1))N?
problemStatement.plain: Erdos #635 asks how dense a subset of {1,...,N} can be when sufficiently separated pairs are forbidden from having their difference divide the larger element.
whyMatters: The problem tests a divisibility restriction that should force asymptotic density at most one half for fixed t.
The Lean file completely handles the t=1 case and basic monotonicity/lower-bound infrastructure.
The general fixed-t asymptotic conjecture remains open and is represented by one explicit axiom.

proven: Lean defines IsNonDivisible, IsAdmissible, the extremal function f(N,t), and oddSet.

Basic infrastructure is proved, including monotonicity in t, trivial upper bounds, half-density lower bounds, and no_far_doubles.
